issues.title: M7.P5: Release versions for the fork — a SemVer scheme for release candidates, so a release is targeted by the features it carries
issues.body:
Maintainer, 2026-09-24 (D-QA-012, D-WORKFLOW-043): *"If, in our Git workflow, we'd like to start using versions more and take some SemVer approach to how we do this (so we can target releases more effectively with the features we hope to include), we can definitely do that, and it might be a good idea. This is the kind of thing I would include in the release following what we're working on now."*

## Current work — 2026-10-10

Child #530's source implementation is delivered on next at f10eec13067a69e3a5670a0879736801b40d2fc0, with both original hosted checks passed. Its next assembled-image criterion remains open. #531 fixes the pre-existing USB calendar-version consumer before that build.

New child #532 owns the requested thin rolling-release naming policy before candidate freeze: evaluate only public RCs and releases, with no required alpha/beta stages. Proposed examples are 0.0.1-rc.1 then 0.0.1; the exact RC counter/promotion/default semantics are not yet selected. Engineering builds retain their honest qualification status. Existing UTC/source metadata and immutable artifact identity remain required. This replaces the earlier intention to leave the whole channel question for later; it does not introduce a multi-stage release pipeline.

#533 under #344 reconciles the remaining candidate issue/evidence scope. This parent retains actual manifest-bound publication, release contents/notes, and the first published version. tools/fork-publish-release now prepares a verified local JSON plan only; the historical newest/date/undraft implementation described below was retired by #530. Naming never confers RC qualification or publication approval.

## Historical disposition — 2026-10-07

The historical request below predates the first fork release. D-CLOUD-157, D-WORKFLOW-094/116 and D-WORKFLOW-144 now identify **pixelelated 0.0.1** as the current release, with rolling 0.0.x updates and BUILD_ID identifying the exact bytes. Milestone7 already targets this version. Do not defer this release's versioned publication work because the original September request referred to the following release.

The image-side version exists: `distributions/ROCKNIX/version` sets `OS_VERSION="0.0.1"`, and the accepted #500 installed readback records that version beside `BUILD_ID="43d0bc3bf47fd858ba8d5c55fbdf52535a0db2aa"`. The retained candidate16 clean/upgraded INFORMATION frames also show `0.0.1 (community)` beside `ee01490 (build/m7-pixelelated-replacement16)`; both original frames and their accepted hashes were re-read. These prove installed identity and its displayed version; they do not prove a new release tag or the completed publication path. The current `tools/fork-publish-release` still selects newest `target/ROCKNIX-*` files, defaults to a date tag and undrafts releases. That path must be reconciled with D-WORKFLOW-120 and #344 before use for 0.0.1.

## Current acceptance criteria

- [ ] Complete #532's focused RC/release naming policy and executable examples, including rolling patch increments, the RC counter and exact-artifact promotion semantics. Existing 0.0.1/rolling 0.0.x and BUILD_ID roles stay settled; alpha/beta stages are not required.
- [x] The installed image and INFORMATION screen carry the selected version and exact build identity: `docs/qa-logs/2026-10-07-device-builds/rg35xxsp-adoption01/reboot-installed-readback.txt` records `OS_VERSION="0.0.1"` and the accepted `BUILD_ID`; `reboot-acceptance.json` and `reboot-owner-verification.json` bind that completed adoption proof. Candidate16 `qa-20/artifacts/identity-initial-clean/03-information.png` and `identity-upgrade/03-information.png`, under `docs/qa-logs/2026-10-07-pixelelated-replacement-16/`, prove the clean/upgraded display; their accepted frame hashes are in `qa20-acceptance/identity-frame-review.json`.
- [ ] The publication path selects the requested version and qualified assets from their immutable manifest, retains draft state until the named publication action, and passes controls for wrong/stale inputs and unqualified assets. A date-tag override alone does not establish this behavior.
- [ ] Document how a release's contents are read from its version milestone, linked issue criteria and final release notes. M7 targeting exists; the final published contents/release-note path remains to be completed under #344.
- [ ] Apply the first completed versioned publication to pixelelated 0.0.1, preserving the selected WebKitGTK 2.54.1 input and its accepted qualification. Compilation and an installed version field alone do not tick publication.

## Historical request and initial task — 2026-09-24

The original timing, identity and task description below are preserved as historical context. The current checklist above is the actionable contract; original maintainer quotations are unchanged.

### What existed on 2026-09-24

- An image's identity is its **BUILD_ID**, the commit `next` was at when the build worktree synced (`build-id-is-the-synced-head`), shown on the device's info screen with the branch name. Cuts are counted in prose on the round issue ("the twenty-first cut", #236) and in `docs/vm-qa-log.md` rows.
- `tools/fork-publish-release` tags a published image `dev-<yyyymmdd>` (one release per build, not per device; the older `dev-<device>-<date>` tags predate that); re-publishing the same day replaces assets under an unchanged tag (blindspot 2).
- Upstream ROCKNIX versions its releases by date (`OS_VERSION` from `distributions/ROCKNIX/version`); the fork carries no version of its own.
- Milestones (`Stable before upstream`, `Offline RetroAchievements`, `Cloud Saves: ...`) group issues by programme, not by release.

### Original task

A versioning scheme for the fork's release candidates and releases, SemVer-shaped, so that an issue can carry the version it is targeted at and a build can say which version it is a candidate for:

1. **The scheme**: what MAJOR, MINOR and PATCH mean for a fork of a date-versioned distribution (a proposal: MINOR per release candidate series, PATCH per cut within it, MAJOR reserved for the upstream base moving); where the pre-release label goes (`-rc.N`); how the version relates to BUILD_ID (both shown; the version names the intent, the id names the bytes).
2. **Where it lives**: a git tag per cut or per candidate on `next`; the version in the image (`/etc/os-release`, the info screen) beside BUILD_ID; `tools/fork-publish-release` tagging by version rather than by date.
3. **How work is targeted**: a milestone or label per version, so "what goes in 0.4.0" is a query; the round issue's contents table (#236's shape) becomes the version's changelog.
4. **The first version**: the release candidate now being cut is the reference point -- named retroactively or the first one named, the maintainer's call.

### Original checklist (historical; superseded above)

- Originally open: A decision-register row fixes the scheme (what each component means, the pre-release form, the relation to BUILD_ID) after the maintainer's word.
- Originally open: A build's image carries its version where BUILD_ID is shown today, and `tools/fork-publish-release` tags by it.
- Originally open: Issues can be targeted at a version (milestone or label), and the fork's docs say how a version's contents are read.
- Originally open: Applied first to the release following the one being cut now (the maintainer: *"the release following what we're working on now"*), with webkitgtk 2.54 (#228, D-WORKFLOW-042) as one of its named features.

full_comments.body: Left for the next release (2026-09-25, the maintainer's choice of "Leave it for next"), as D-WORKFLOW-043 already says: the scheme is settled when the next candidate's work begins, this candidate stays known by its build ID `664ad9ac64`, and it can still be given a number retroactively then (the fourth item of the task).

issues.title: M7.P3: The fork's own identity — the name, the branding the licence requires, sponsorships without a community, the site and the releases
issues.body:
## P4 contract reconciliation — 2026-10-06

Read the complete issue comment history and settled decisions before this edit. This reconciles stale directory/site/grep/organization requirements; it does not tick runtime acceptance or close the issue. Published source repairs and candidate15 evidence remain under audit#471, with four findings resolved and four open. A rebuilt image and remaining installed qualification precede the RC call; H700 and P5 publication evidence remain separate. The milestone body owns the current order.

## Current identity transition — 2026-10-04

#409 is first within M7.P3 before the next freeze/build: lowercase **pixelelated**, organization `pixelelated`, owner `rasteratops`, unchanged developer `blitterbot`, default `/pixelelated`. Rasteratops remains a character. D-WORKFLOW-144/D-CLOUD-174 supersede earlier project/default naming below. The owner confirms no systems use `/Rasteratops`: **ROCKNIX → pixelelated** is the required adoption path. Existing cloud folders may move through the established verified migration. Historical replacement02 remains RASTERATOPS evidence; new bytes require new qualification. The milestone body owns the order, followed by remaining P3 checks, expanded P4 fixes audit and separately gated P5.

## Historical source checkpoint — 2026-10-02 (#385)

This dated checkpoint and the original proposal below predate D-WORKFLOW-144. They are historical context, not current implementation instructions. The active contract retains `DISTRO=ROCKNIX`, `distributions/ROCKNIX/` and RC2 stored interfaces (D-WORKFLOW-123), uses manual updates, and limits the website to the approved name-only placeholder. Current execution and remaining gates are in M7 and #471.

Distribution fcd0f20c9a (next df23faff6c) pins ES 97523542963dcc72e9ea51cfbcd26b735ff28c1f and splash 7450aa8180ae66684814dd460f31eb502b2abf61. RASTERATOPS/0.0.1, wordmark, manual updater, reporting disablement and licence files exist in source; there is no branded candidate image yet. D-WORKFLOW-093 selects manual adoption; the site is the approved placeholder (D-WORKFLOW-098), not a new full-site gate. Legacy cloud names remain where compatibility readers/migration need them. See docs/rasteratops/release-readiness.md.

**Maintainer, 2026-09-29 (chat, D-QA-012), and later the same evening on sponsorships:** *"I also don't need to accept sponsorship. I really don't care either way. If at some point I wanted a Patreon or something, I could do that. This is more about whether it would be about sponsoring my work, but then that's just actually creating more issues because I have sponsors to deal with. Let's strike that concept: no sponsorships here."* The first message: *"At a certain point, it might be easier to fork, create the version I want, not allow for contributors, enable GitHub sponsorships, and just quietly offer an alternative. I have no interest in a Discord server, managing a community, etc., but I am interested in having a better experience, even if it's mainly just for me. If others can enjoy it, all the better, but to put in a lot of work and then not have it upstreamed seems silly. I also have a name we could use for this."* -- *"pixelelated", where I own the domain as well.*

**Historical initial proposal**, from #334's licence read. The numbered proposal below is retained for provenance; its directory rename, automatic updater endpoint, full website and old decision gate were superseded by D-WORKFLOW-093/098/123/144. The acceptance criteria below are the current requirements.

1. **The name in the tree**: `distributions/ROCKNIX/` becomes `distributions/pixelelated/` (the options file's `DISTRONAME`, `OS_NAME`, the version), the update URL the updater reads pointed at the fork's own releases, the theme's logo and the splash replaced by artwork of the fork's own (the ROCKNIX images may not be reused as a fork's identity), the device pages' names where they say ROCKNIX, and a line in the fork's README and release notes: *a fork of ROCKNIX, itself a fork of JELOS*, with the credits kept whole. The kernel, bootloaders, device trees, quirks and every package stay as merged from `upstream/next`.
2. **The repositories**: the distribution fork renamed to match (GitHub redirects the old name), the EmulationStation fork likewise; issues on, pull requests unsolicited (a public repository cannot refuse them; a `CONTRIBUTING.md` says the project takes none and the template says so), no sponsorships of any kind (struck by the maintainer, below), no Discord and no community channel -- the releases page and the site are the whole surface.
3. **The site**: the domain the maintainer owns, a MkDocs site like rocknix.org's from the pages already written for it (`docs/configure/cloud-sync.md`, `networking.md`, `play/retro-achievements.md` in the site checkout), under the new name, in the maintainer's voice.
4. **The releases**: the same `tools/fork-publish-release` and notes as RC1 and RC2, under the new tag prefix and name; every image built from one head, proven on the VM first, on the devices with a yes.

Can this be done on the VM? Yes: an image that boots under the new name with its own splash on guest d is the proof; a device after, on its yes.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The register row that calls the direction (D-WORKFLOW-081's answer) names the fork's name and the licence terms it keeps (GPL-2 and MIT kept whole; the CC BY-SA attribution line; no ROCKNIX images).
- [ ] A GENERIC_X64 image boots under the new name with its own splash and logo, `OS_NAME` read from `/etc/os-release`, the manual-update row visible, and no automatic upstream update request in the captured guest network evidence (frame/readback/capture filed here).
- [ ] P5 site item #345: the approved placeholder at pixelelated.com shows the lowercase name only, per D-WORKFLOW-098; retain its build and retrieval receipt when deployed. Lineage, licence and adoption information belongs in the separately tracked release/public documentation. A full website is not a 0.0.1 gate.




## Historical cloud-root decision — current default superseded by D-CLOUD-174

The October1 quotation and description below record the earlier /Rasteratops proposal. Active defaults and required adoption are /pixelelated and ROCKNIX → pixelelated; the checkbox contract below uses the current decision.

> let's move everything to "/Rasteratops" as the default root directory we look for. that should be part of our baseline brand transition

So the identity change carries the cloud folder with the name, the splash, the version and the strings: `cloud_sync.conf` and `.defaults` ship `/Rasteratops/Saves`, `/Rasteratops/Backups`, `/Rasteratops/Content` (`SAVES_REMOTE`, `SETTINGS_REMOTE`, `CONTENT_REMOTE`, and `DEFAULT_*`), `cloud_setup`'s derived paths, the wizard's and the transfer page's words, `cloud_migrate_layout`'s target, the device-name fallbacks and the `/ROCKNIX` strings in the interface (`GuiMenu.cpp:5230`) read the new name; the migrations and guards are #353's.

- [ ] A fresh guest on the candidate, signed in to the QA cloud, creates and uses `/pixelelated/{Saves,Backups,Content}`: `tools/cloud-test-backend ls` after a backup and a saves sync shows the three folders and nothing under `/ROCKNIX`; the active `SAVES_REMOTE`, `SETTINGS_REMOTE`, `CONTENT_REMOTE` and corresponding `DEFAULT_*` assignments in `cloud_sync.conf`/`.defaults` name those exact paths; retained `ROCKNIX_SETTINGS` archive-format comments remain valid compatibility documentation; `tools/vocabulary-check` passes.
- [ ] Retain an explicit disposition for all 56 historical `cloud-path` entries from `docs/rasteratops/p0-sweep-hits.txt`, naming the original baseline and each current path/value/classification. The retrospective mapping in `docs/qa-logs/2026-10-06-pixelelated-replacement-15/cloud-path-disposition/` is not a claim that all dispositions were made in the old baseline commit. The candidate source/artifact sweep has zero unclassified or incorrect active-default contexts; valid legacy readers, upstream URLs, build identifiers and historical comments remain intact.


## Added 2026-10-01: the case, the placeholder mark, the tar's name, the password note (D-WORKFLOW-127 to 130)

> Our convention might be better in the OS release to either be lowercase or uppercase. I'm fine either way, but the general convention looks good. I'm happy with whatever you recommend there.

> I'm still working on the artwork. In the short term, maybe we just use a word mark without an icon until I have one as a placeholder.

- [ ] `DISTRONAME="pixelelated"`: `os-release` reads `OS_NAME="pixelelated"`, the images are `pixelelated-<board>.<arch>-0.0.1.*`, the info page reads `OPERATING SYSTEM: pixelelated` (a 640x480 frame from guest d; `/etc/os-release` from the image's SYSTEM); the GitHub organization and product display identity are lowercase `pixelelated`, the maintainer is `rasteratops` and developer `blitterbot` is unchanged (D-WORKFLOW-144); RC2 stored identifiers remain under D-WORKFLOW-123, and the cloud default is `/pixelelated` (D-CLOUD-174).
- [ ] The migration tar carries the suffix `-from-ROCKNIX` (`IMAGE_SUFFIX`), so its name passes the RC2 init's check (`init:882`): the built name is `pixelelated-H700.aarch64-0.0.1-from-ROCKNIX.tar` and `tools/vm-upgrade-rehearsal` from RC2's image applies it; the suffix is dropped in the build after 0.0.1 (D-WORKFLOW-128).
- [ ] The splash and the theme's logo carry the word mark alone until the icon arrives (D-WORKFLOW-130): the splash frame at boot and the theme's logo frame on guest d show lowercase pixelelated in Tiny5 Duo LCD, with the approved Ocean Bands treatment and no pictorial mark (D-WORKFLOW-145).
- [ ] The release notes and the site's ssh page say the ssh password is unchanged in 0.0.1 (D-WORKFLOW-129, #358): the notes file's line and the docs PR.

full_comments.body:
**Maintainer, 2026-09-29, the last word on the identity for now:** *"I don't even love GitHub, and so if we were to self-host something like JJ or Forgejo, I'd be fine with that. I think the more control we have over the stack, the better."*

Noted as part of the fork's footing, not started. What it touches when it comes, read from the tree: the issue tracker (every `gh issue` call in the session tooling and the D-QA-012 paper trail live on GitHub issues; Forgejo's issues and API are close enough that `tools/box-check`, `tools/archaeology` and the sub-issue calls move with a client change), the releases (`tools/fork-publish-release` uses `gh release`; Forgejo has releases and an API), the CI (`.github/workflows/fork-checks.yml` is GitHub Actions; Forgejo Actions runs most of the same workflow syntax), the push guard (`.githooks/pre-push` is git's own hook and moves anywhere git does; **Jujutsu's push does not run git hooks**, so on jj the guard is re-homed into CI or a server-side hook, which Forgejo has), and the update path (the updater reads a releases page; the fork's own is whatever it points at). The estate already runs a Forgejo, which is the natural home. None of it blocks the rename or the runner; it is a move the tooling can make one client at a time.

**Maintainer, 2026-09-29:** *"If we need GitHub, that's fine too."* -- so the host is not a constraint either way; the fork stays on GitHub until moving buys something, and the tooling is kept host-agnostic where that is cheap.

**Maintainer, 2026-09-29:** *"Honestly, I'm happy building a better OS, even if it's just used by me. I have a feeling that there's a divergence of opinion, and I don't want to waste my time trying to figure out how to work with their system. We'll see what they come back with, but I kind of feel at this point we have a strong release candidate. We might be better off referring to this as version 0.0.1 of our new OS than considering it something we upstream."*

**What "0.0.1 of the new OS" is, in the tree, read tonight.** The name lives in five files under `distributions/ROCKNIX/` (`options` sets `DISTRONAME`, `version` sets `DISTRO_VERSION` and `OS_VERSION`, `logos/rocknix-logo.png`, `kernel_options`, `config/functions`); the updater asks an update endpoint by POST and follows the address it returns, so the fork's own endpoint or release page goes there; the boot splash and the theme's logo text are the artwork. RC2's images boot as ROCKNIX with ROCKNIX's logo, so they can be *called* 0.0.1 privately today and *published* as the new OS only after the rename and the artwork (the branding's licence). A rename is about a day: a `distributions/<name>/` with the four files and a wordmark, `OS_VERSION` as `0.0.1`, the updater's address, the theme patch's text, then the four images rebuilt from one head, the VM suites and the rehearsal, and the devices on a yes. The fork's release page carries `0.0.1` beside `rc2-20260929` with the attribution line.

**Version scheme, proposed:** `0.0.1` for this cut, `0.0.x` for fixes on it, `0.1` for the first cut that carries the fork's own direction (#336's step 0), so the number says what the build is rather than when it was made -- the date stays in the file names as now.

Nothing starts until the maintainer calls D-WORKFLOW-081; the generic fixes go to their own upstreams regardless, and one small PR to ROCKNIX is all *"see what they come back with"* costs.

**Maintainer, 2026-09-30:** *"I think I'm going to call it, 'rasteratops'. thoughts?"* -- Checked: no repository, user or organisation on GitHub matches it (0, 0, 0), and the web has no project by that name; the nearest is RasterOps, a Macintosh graphics-card maker founded in 1987 and long since renamed, and the rest of the results are ceratopsian dinosaurs. Eleven letters against ROCKNIX's seven, which the wordmark and the file names carry fine. *raster* is the pixel grid and the CRT scan, *-atops* the horned dinosaur, which hands the fork its logo: a pixel triceratops. The domain is the one thing not checked here. The name goes into D-WORKFLOW-081's deciding row when the maintainer confirms it.

**Maintainer, 2026-09-30:** *"i could also go with Rasteroid/RasteroidOS"* -- Checked: **rasteroid** is taken in every direction -- 17 GitHub repositories (Asteroids clones, a game controller, a sound server), 4 users or organisations including the user `rasteroid`, a solo game developer of that name on itch.io and GitHub, a former OpenGL ES middleware product called Rasteroid by Hybrid (Khronos news), a design studio and Instagram account called Rasteroids, and a SoundCloud artist. **RasteroidOS** has no match anywhere, but it lives one letter from all of the above and would be searched as *rasteroid*. **rasteratops** has zero matches on GitHub and none on the web. On collisions alone, rasteratops; the maintainer's ear decides the rest.

**Decided (D-WORKFLOW-084):** the fork is **rasteratops**. Maintainer, 2026-09-30: *"rasteratops it is. let me grab the GitHub org."* Phase B's organisation is the maintainer's; Phase A (the identity in the tree, on the VM first) follows the council's sitting on #338.

**Maintainer, 2026-09-30:** *"we can use this for the splash screen, until we have a logo: https://github.com/gissio/font_tiny5"* -- Tiny5 (gissio), a family of 5-pixel fonts under the SIL Open Font License 1.1, shipped as variable TTF/OTF and as BDF bitmaps, with a heavier *Tiny5 Duo* for titles; the OFL asks only that the font files keep their notice when redistributed, and an image rendered with it carries no obligation. The interim wordmark: *rasteratops* in Tiny5 Duo, one pixel per font pixel scaled by a whole number, centred on black at each panel size. The splash itself is a separate ROCKNIX repository (`rocknix-splash`, GPL, a small application pinned by commit in `projects/ROCKNIX/packages/tools/rocknix-splash/package.mk`), so Phase A forks that repository into the organisation, replaces its image with the wordmark, and points the recipe at the fork's commit.

**The interim wordmark is rendered** (`/workspace/tmp/rocknix-session/splash/`, not in the tree until Phase A): *rasteratops* in Tiny5 Duo from the font's own BDF bitmap, 58 x 6 font pixels, scaled nine times to 522 x 54 on a 640 x 480 black canvas, light grey; a 640 x 480 PNG preview and an SVG of 146 one-pixel squares. The splash application (`ROCKNIX/rocknix-splash`) draws no image file: its logo is SVG path data compiled into `main.c` (`svg_paths[]`, seven letter paths, four red and three grey) rendered by its own parser, which understands M, L, H, V, Z and cubic curves, and scales the drawing to the panel. So Phase A's splash is a fork of that repository with `svg_paths[]` replaced by the wordmark's one path (146 `M x y h1 v1 h-1 z` squares in a 58 x 6 box, generated and kept beside the preview) in one colour, and the recipe's pin moved to the fork's commit. A pixel triceratops takes the same route when it exists.

**Maintainer, 2026-09-30:** *"We can quickly come up with an SVG if we need to as well of the word rasteratops, looking like a triceratops"* -- Two pixel-art drafts of a triceratops head beside the wordmark are in `/workspace/tmp/rocknix-session/splash/` (`rasteratops-head-640x480.png`, an outline that reads as a rodent; `rasteratops-head2-640x480.png`, a solid silhouette that reads as a beast with a hump but not yet a triceratops). The mechanics are settled by them: any drawing on a pixel grid, up to about 32 x 20 cells, becomes the splash's one path and scales cleanly to every panel; an SVG the maintainer draws drops into the same route. What the animal needs at this size, for whoever draws it: a solid silhouette, not an outline; three horns two cells thick (two long brow horns forward and up, one short nose horn); a frill that stands off the head with a scalloped edge; a beak; one eye. The word stays as Tiny5 Duo draws it, since features worked into the letters read as noise at 640 x 480.

**Maintainer, 2026-09-30:** *"I can do the art. Tell me the resolution you definitely want, and I can work on that. If we're using Tiny 5 Duo, I can create an SVG and optimize for a pixel grid of 32x20 if that's our goal."*

**The panels, read from the devices:** the RG35XX SP, the RG SP, the RG353M and the VM draw at 640 x 480; the Retroid Pocket Nova at 1280 x 960 -- all 4:3, the Nova exactly twice the others. **The splash application** scales by floating point (60 % of the screen's width, a hard-coded 1284:500 aspect, the renderer's `min(scale_x, scale_y)`) with no whole-pixel snap, so its fork gets two one-line changes: the drawing's own box instead of 1284:500, and the scale rounded down to a whole number, so every cell lands on whole pixels.

**The specification, then:**

- **The logo (the animal): a 32 x 20 cell grid.** One main colour; one optional accent colour (the eye, or the horns), since the renderer colours per path; transparent background. Delivered as an SVG with `viewBox="0 0 32 20"` made of 1 x 1 `rect`s or of paths on whole-number coordinates only, no curves, no fractional edges. Facing the word (to the right) reads best beside it; facing left works above it.
- **The wordmark is not drawn:** *rasteratops* comes from Tiny5 Duo's own bitmap, 57 x 6 cells, generated.
- **The composition the splash draws:** a 64 x 32 canvas, the animal centred in rows 0-19, the word centred in rows 24-29. On 640 x 480 the fork's whole-number scale is 6 (384 x 192 on screen); on the Nova 12. The same logo SVG serves the theme's logo text, the release page and the site at any size, since it is cells.

The two drafts under `/workspace/tmp/rocknix-session/splash/` show the composition, not the animal.

**Interim icon received, 2026-10-01** (`docs/rasteratops/art/icon-interim-2026-10-01.png`, `a9de01d050`): the 32 x 20 pixel triceratops, RGBA, 718 bytes, no metadata chunks; purple-and-blue body with cream highlights and a cyan eye; about 170 distinct opaque colours (resampled rather than a fixed palette, which the splash's SVG conversion will flatten per cell). The maintainer: *"This is also going to be revised, but if we need something we can use in the short term, we can use this."* So the placeholder for 0.0.1 is the word mark (D-WORKFLOW-130) with this icon beside it where an icon is wanted, replaced when the revision arrives. Open: the terms for the fork's own branding (ROCKNIX's CC BY-NC-SA section in `LICENSE.md` is replaced, not reused).

issues.body:
## Readiness review update — 2026-10-02 (#375)

D-CLOUD-164's approved offered-row text is `<DEVICE>, <DATE>` without FROM. D-CLOUD-162's same-device restriction applies to the cloud restore selection: it passes the chosen compatible archive to backuptool; the independent local recovery entry point is not redefined here. #376 adds legacy/new OS-name archive compatibility before the final branded image. Reverify the row and actual selected archive on that image. Source/VM evidence is in `docs/audits/2026_10_02-milestone-375-rasteratops-0-0-1/04-analysis.md`; this is a body reconciliation of recorded decisions, not new product policy.

## The maintainer's words (2026-09-30, setting up the Retroid Pocket Nova)

> when it comes to restoring with settings, is there any risk in restoring settings from a different console? I'm about to set up the Pocket Nova, and I'm wondering if I should restore settings because they'd be coming from my RG35XX SP, I'm assuming, or maybe elsewhere. I actually forget the flow. If we allow someone to choose where it's coming from, this is a good lesson, I guess, but immediately I see settings in the toggle, and I'm wondering what happens if it's a different device than the other devices I own.

## What exists today (read from `backuptool` at `224b73ea54`)

- A settings restore takes **the newest archive in the cloud's Backups folder, whichever device made it**: `backuptool:159-161` picks `ls …/*-ROCKNIX_SETTINGS.tar.gz | sort | tail -1`. The archive's name carries the device label (`<stamp>-<label>-ROCKNIX_SETTINGS.tar.gz`, `:143`, D-CLOUD-009) and nothing reads it back on restore. No `HW_DEVICE` comparison exists in the script.
- The archive holds `system.cfg` whole minus credential keys (`:282`, the scrub at `:416`), `retroarch/*`, `es_settings.cfg`, `fancontrol.conf`, `ppsspp/*`, `moonlight/*`, `game/*` (`:280-287`) and the systems' own configs. So the RG35XX SP's archive on the Nova brings its hostname (`system.hostname`; D-NET-001 treats any name that is not the family's as the player's own and keeps it, so the Nova would answer to the SP's name), RetroArch video and scaling settings tuned for a 640x480 H700 panel, and the H700's fan settings.
- A pre-restore snapshot is written first (`:1459`) and `revert_restore` exists (`:662`); the FINISH RESTORE SETUP wizard then asks for what was held back (the Wi-Fi password, the accounts).
- The transfer page's SETTINGS toggle names neither the device the archive came from nor that a choice exists.

Answer given at the time: do not restore the SP's settings onto the Nova; set it up fresh and let saves sync; the Nova's own settings back up from there.

## Can this be done on the VM?

**Yes.** The label is a string in the file name: `tools/cloud-test-backend seed-content` puts two labelled archives (say `Anbernic-RG35XX-SP` and `Retroid-Pocket-Nova`) in the QA cloud's Backups folder, and guest d restores as the second device. Nothing here needs a board.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] On the transfer page, the SETTINGS restore row's line under the label names the device the archive to be restored came from, read from the label in its file name (`backuptool` prints it; the interface reads it): a 640x480 frame from a `tools/vm-walks` walk shows `<DEVICE>, <DATE>` (D-CLOUD-164).
- ~~When the Backups folder holds archives from more than one device label, the restore asks which device's settings to restore (a page, not a third line: D-UI-023), defaulting to this device's own newest; a frame shows the choice with both labels.~~ *Superseded by D-CLOUD-156 and D-CLOUD-162 (no choice page; only this device's own backup is offered), below.*
- ~~A restore from another device's archive is confirmed with the device named and the held-back list stated (YES first; back lands on NO: `es-ui-style-guide.md`); a frame shows the dialog's text.~~ *Superseded by D-CLOUD-156 and D-CLOUD-162 (no choice page; only this device's own backup is offered), below.*
- ~~A cross-device restore leaves `system.hostname`, `fancontrol.conf` and the RetroArch video-driver keys as they were on the restoring device: after the VM restore of the seeded foreign archive, `get_setting system.hostname` on guest d is unchanged and `backuptool`'s journal names each held-back file.~~ *Superseded by D-CLOUD-156 and D-CLOUD-162 (no choice page; only this device's own backup is offered), below.*
- [ ] `docs/es-menu-map.md` carries the SETTINGS row's two states, offered with the device and date or dimmed with `NO SETTINGS BACKUP FROM THIS DEVICE YET` (D-UI-039, D-CLOUD-162), and `tools/es-menu-map-check` passes in `tools/vm-qa`'s `menumap` suite. *(Rewritten 2026-10-01: the choice page it named is superseded.)*
- [ ] The public page for cloud sync says the SETTINGS row restores this device's own newest backup and is dimmed when the cloud has none from it (docs follow-up with #42, `documentation-accuracy.md`). *(Rewritten 2026-10-01: a restore from another device is not offered.)*

## Design, 2026-09-30 (D-CLOUD-156): scan first, then offer only what this device can restore

The maintainer, later the same evening: *"if we knew that I'm on a Retroid Pocket Nova, we shouldn't show the option if there isn't a Retroid Pocket Nova backup available. Maybe the scanning the cloud step should come first, and that way we can only offer options that we can actually support in the backup. We'd have the screen real estate during the scan to also be able to say, 'We're checking to see what device-specific content and settings are available,' or something like that."*

So the per-device choice page proposed above is not the shape. The scan page (#350) runs first; the settings row is offered only when the cloud holds a settings archive whose label is this device model's (`cloud_device_id --label`, the label in the archive's name), and otherwise reads its reason. One open point for the maintainer: `es-ui-style-guide.md` dims a row that has nothing to offer rather than hiding it (`NO SETTINGS BACKUP FROM THIS DEVICE YET`, dimmed); their words say "shouldn't show the option". The row is written dimmed unless they say absent. The criteria above that describe a choice page are superseded by these:

- [ ] After the scan page (#350), the SETTINGS restore row is offered only when the cloud's Backups folder holds an archive whose label equals this device's `cloud_device_id --label`; with the QA cloud seeded with a foreign label only, guest d's 640x480 frame shows the row dimmed with its reason, and with its own label seeded the row is offered with `<DEVICE>, <DATE>` (D-CLOUD-164) under it.
- [ ] A restore never takes another device's archive by default: the cloud restore selects this device model's newest compatible archive and passes it to `backuptool`, and its journal line names the label it chose; the foreign-label case on guest d leaves `system.hostname` unchanged.
- [ ] The scan page's line reads, while it runs, the words approved for #350 (proposed: `CHECKING WHAT SETTINGS AND CONTENT YOUR CLOUD HAS FOR THIS DEVICE...`), and the outcome vocabulary when it ends (`es-player-text.md`); frames from the walk show both.

The CONTENT TO RESTORE flow confirms with a dialog and then draws the comparison's busy card over it while `cloud_content_restore` lists the cloud (the loader text is `COMPARING YOUR CLOUD'S CONTENT WITH THIS DEVICE`). full_comments.body:
## Design, 2026-10-01: the scan page is the transfer page running a scan script

Read before designing: `GuiCloudTransfer` is this codebase's page for a job a player sits in (D-UI-078): a title, a live line from `>>> unit <label>|<i>|<n>` lines, `>>> why` for the outcome's reason, CANCEL as the one way out, the outcome vocabulary at the end, and `setCompletedAction` for what happens next (`GuiCloudTransfer.cpp:25-60,178`; `CloudTransferJob.cpp` § handleLine). `CloudText::transferKind` picks the verb from the command (`BACKING UP...`, `RESTORING...`, `MATCHING...`, else `WORKING...`; `CloudText.cpp:641`). The content picker today is a `GuiLoading` card over the dialog (`GuiMenu.cpp:4186-4200`), the surface the maintainer met.

So the page is not new code: it is `GuiCloudTransfer(window, "/usr/bin/cloud_scan", _("CHECKING YOUR CLOUD"))` with a completed action that opens the options page.

- **`cloud_scan`** (new, in the rclone package): runs, in order, `cloud_migrate_layout --state` (the folder: current, kept, superseded, own), the settings archives in the cloud by device label (from `SETTINGS_REMOTE`, the label in each name), `cloud_setup --content-location`, and `cloud_content_restore --scan`; prints `>>> unit FOLDER||`, `>>> unit SETTINGS||`, `>>> unit CONTENT||` as each begins and `>>> why <sentence>` where one fails; writes each result to `/storage/.cache/cloud_sync/scan/<name>` and a `done` stamp; exits 0, 69 (no network) or the failing part's code. This is not the right path. I have no way to remedy it, and it's letting me select whether or not I want to restore content totally unrelated to my gameplay experience.

## What exists today (read from `cloud_content_restore` and `cloud_setup` at `224b73ea54`)

- CONTENT TO RESTORE is built from `cloud_content_restore --scan` (`GuiMenu.cpp:4196`). The scan lists `${ROOT}ROMs/` and `${ROOT}BIOS/` (`:1243,1256`), and then **appends every top-level folder under `${ROOT}` that holds files** as a "pre-tier layout" row with no comparison and no filter (`sizes_under "${ROOT}" | grep -vE '^(ROMs|BIOS)|'`, `:1298`, emitted at `:1337-1341`). `ROOT` is the remote's root when `CONTENT_REMOTE` is empty (`:207`), so on a device whose content root is the Dropbox root the page lists the account's own folders as systems to restore.
- The filter the script's own comments promise ("Only directories this device actually has locally are offered from there -- listing somebody's holiday photos as restorable ROMs would be worse than the empty list this fixes", `:356-358` and `:398-400`) exists in `resolve_src` (`legacy_dirs`, `:404-411`) and is **not applied by `--scan`**. A name is not a behaviour (`engineering-practices.md`).
- `cloud_setup --content-location` reports `STATE=stranded-at-root|ok|empty` and `--use-content-root` sets `CONTENT_REMOTE` to empty (`cloud_setup:495-556`), and a fresh image ships `CONTENT_REMOTE="/ROCKNIX/Content"` (`cloud_sync.conf:46`). Which of these put the Nova's content root at the Dropbox root is a device read still owed (its address did not resolve from serval at the time).
- There is no row in the interface to choose the content folder: `CHANGE CLOUD FOLDER` was removed with the NETWORK SETTINGS group and "reproduced nowhere" (`engineering-practices.md` § Before deleting a duplicate). The maintainer's "I have no way to remedy it" is that gap.

Answer given at the time: restore nothing from that list; a run there would copy the listed folders under `/storage/roms/<name>/`.

## Can this be done on the VM?

**Yes.** `tools/cloud-test-backend seed-content` puts a `Photos/` and a `Documents/` folder beside `/ROCKNIX/Content` (and at the root) in the QA cloud; guest d with `CONTENT_REMOTE=""` and with the default reproduces both listings; the page's frame at 640x480 is the observation.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `cloud_content_restore --scan` lists a pre-tier folder only when this device has a folder of that name under `/storage/roms` or the name is a supported system (`legacy_dirs` / `supported_systems`), the same rule `resolve_src` applies; a `tools/cloud-round-trip` case seeds `Photos/` and `Documents/` at the root and the scan's output carries neither line.
- [ ] When the content root holds no `ROMs/` and no known system folder, the page says so instead of listing: `YOUR CLOUD HAS NO ROMS OR BIOS AT <folder>.` / `CHOOSE THE FOLDER WHERE YOUR GAMES ARE?` (approved D-CLOUD-164), with a row that opens the folder chooser; a 640x480 frame shows it.
- [ ] A CHOOSE CLOUD FOLDER page (the `GuiFileBrowser` pattern fed by `rclone lsf`, `es-native-ui.md` § Reusable precedents) sets `CONTENT_REMOTE` through `cloud_setup`, and the transfer page re-reads it; the walk's frames show the chosen folder and the journal shows the `Content path` line.
- [ ] With `CONTENT_REMOTE` back at `/ROCKNIX/Content` and the QA cloud seeded with `Photos/` and `Documents/` at its root, CONTENT TO RESTORE on guest d lists only ROM systems and BIOS: the walk's 640x480 frame and the scan's output lines. (The Nova's own listing is re-read on its next staging, as a read, and noted here in a comment.)
- [ ] `docs/es-menu-map.md` carries the chooser (D-UI-039); `tools/es-menu-map-check` and `tools/vocabulary-check` pass; the cloud-sync page on the site says where the content folder is chosen (`documentation-accuracy.md`).

## Design, 2026-09-30 (D-CLOUD-156): find the folder under the cloud root before asking

The maintainer, later the same evening: *"we could be more intelligent with identifying the appropriate folder if it's not at the root, like mine isn't, because it all goes in the Rocknix directory. That's where I thought it would be looking, and so we should be scanning that."* And: *"certainly making sure we're not showing content that's not relevant to Rasteratops."*

So the chooser is the last resort, not the first answer. Added criteria, ahead of the chooser's:

- [ ] When the configured content root holds no `ROMs/` and no known system folder, the scan looks under the cloud root's `/ROCKNIX/Content` (the saves root's parent, `cloud_setup:629-631`) and, finding `ROMs/` or `BIOS/` there, uses that folder automatically and writes `CONTENT_REMOTE` (D-CLOUD-167, no USE IT confirmation); on guest d with `CONTENT_REMOTE=""` and content seeded under `/ROCKNIX/Content`, the frame sequence advances to the options and the journal shows the `Content path` line.
- [ ] Only then, with nothing found under either, the chooser opens; a frame shows it with the QA cloud's root folders listed as folders to pick from, never as systems.

issues.title: M7.P3: The saves-folder offer names upstream's /GAMES on a device upgraded from stock ROCKNIX; show it after the sign-in, with a folder choice
issues.body:
## Current identity transition — 2026-10-04

#409 is first within M7.P3 before the next freeze/build: lowercase **pixelelated**, organization `pixelelated`, owner `rasteratops`, unchanged developer `blitterbot`, default `/pixelelated`. Rasteratops remains a character. D-WORKFLOW-144/D-CLOUD-174 supersede earlier project/default naming below. The owner confirms no systems use `/Rasteratops`: **ROCKNIX → pixelelated** is the required adoption path. Existing cloud folders may move through the established verified migration. Historical replacement02 remains RASTERATOPS evidence; new bytes require new qualification. The milestone body owns the order, followed by remaining P3 checks, expanded P4 fixes audit and separately gated P5.

## The maintainer's words (2026-09-30, the Retroid Pocket Nova's first boots on RC2)

> I just turned on the console, and an odd screen appeared, which I hadn't seen before. It says, "Your cloud has no /games folder yet. Create it now" and "Create it" and "Not now" as options. The screen needs to be formatted differently because there's a question mark separating the two rows of text.
>
> Also, I'd expect this screen to be shown immediately after linking a cloud provider. We also should give someone the option of choosing a different directory if all of their contents are already in a different location. Additionally, instead of saying a /games folder, we might want to move to a /Rasteratops folder.

## What exists today, and the cause (read from the device and the code, 2026-09-30)

- The screen is the saves-folder offer: `cloud_restore:1729` prints `>>> offer create-saves-folder|<saves folder>` when the configured saves folder is absent but its parent lists, and `CloudOffer.cpp:59-64` shows `YOUR CLOUD HAS NO %s FOLDER YET.\n\nCREATE IT NOW?` with CREATE IT / NOT NOW. It runs from the startup sync (`GuiCloudTransfer.cpp:297`), which is why it appeared at a boot and not after the sign-in.
- **The folder it names is upstream ROCKNIX's shipped default, not ours.** The Nova ran stock ROCKNIX 20260901 before RC1, and stock ships `SYNCPATH="/GAMES"` (`upstream/next:cloud_sync.conf:18`). The fork's `cloud_sync_helper` renames the keys and keeps the values on purpose (`:393-395`, `:467-473`: *"an upgrading device keeps whatever it had - '/GAMES' for anyone set…"*, D-WORKFLOW-101's "configured root wins on upgrade"). Read from the Nova (`rocknix_ed25519`, a read): `SAVES_REMOTE="/GAMES"`, `SETTINGS_REMOTE="/GAMES/backup"`, `CONTENT_REMOTE=""` (`/storage/.config/cloud_sync.conf:67-69`, written 2026-09-29 15:35 EDT at RC1's first boot); the Dropbox holds `/ROCKNIX/{Backups,Content,Saves,Saves-replaced}` and **no `/GAMES`**. So the device offers to create a folder the player never chose beside the one their other devices use, and its content root, empty, is the Dropbox root: **this is the cause of #352's listing too.**
- A `/GAMES` typed by hand is refused (`cloud_setup:350-366`: the saves folder needs a parent); a `/GAMES` carried across an upgrade is never checked.
- The dialog's icon is `ICON_AUTOMATIC` (`GuiMsgBox.h:15`), chosen by the trailing `?`; the "question mark separating the two rows" is that icon's placement at the Nova's panel size, to be seen on a frame.

The remedy on the Nova tonight is one line on the maintainer's yes: `cloud_setup --set-saves-remote /ROCKNIX/Saves` writes the three fork paths (`cloud_setup:629-631`) and moves nothing in the cloud.

## Can this be done on the VM?

**Yes.** Guest d boots the previous stock-shaped conf (`SYNCPATH="/GAMES"`) through `tools/vm-upgrade-rehearsal`'s seeding, with the QA cloud holding `/ROCKNIX/Saves` and no `/GAMES`; the offer's frame at 640x480 and the journal are the observation. The naming question is the maintainer's.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A carried upstream `/GAMES` (a value no player typed) counts as no folder (D-CLOUD-161). At the end of cloud setup the seeding points it at `/pixelelated` and makes the three folders without asking (D-CLOUD-169: `tools/last-good-scripts-test`'s `--settle` lines); at boot the cloud folder step offers CREATE IT / CHOOSE A FOLDER / NOT NOW (D-CLOUD-170: guest d's epic proof, case E's frame), and so does a transfer page's scan, where CREATE IT writes the three `/pixelelated` paths (case B: the conf's three lines and `tools/cloud-test-backend ls`); with a `/GAMES` that holds files the dialog is the move naming `/GAMES` (case B0's frame).
- [ ] An earlier `/ROCKNIX` folder gets one dialog, MOVE first (D-CLOUD-160): MOVE copies, verifies and deletes (the move page's frames on guest d; `tools/cloud-test-backend ls` shows `/pixelelated` whole and no `/ROCKNIX`; a kill during the copy leaves `/ROCKNIX` intact and a second MOVE completes it); another device on `/ROCKNIX` is re-pointed at its next cloud folder step or transfer-page scan with no dialog (`tools/cloud-pair-migration` step 5's journal line, D-CLOUD-170), one that wrote there first is merged by its MOVE (step 5m, D-CLOUD-168); KEEP USING leaves a device on `/ROCKNIX` for good; NOT NOW asks again at the next boot and the next transfer page.
- [ ] The folder is settled by the cloud folder step, at the end of cloud setup and at boot (D-CLOUD-170, #363). Ordinary backup/restore and exit-sync paths do not run networked layout preparation. D-CLOUD-173 permits the boot worker to prepare eligible legacy pointers through the existing join/state/follow scan before startup transfers, with a 30-second ceiling; failed preparation ends the worker before transfer and moves no cloud files. The setup dialog waits for the worker and actual notification linger/fade to finish. Outside that bounded boot preparation, with the folder absent the startup and exit syncs end in the card's `SKIPPED - YOUR CLOUD FOLDER ISN'T SET UP YET` pointing at MANAGE CLOUD STORAGE (the startup stamp's `78 no-folder`, D-CLOUD-166), and 640x480 frames show the step at the end of setup (guest d's epic proof, case L) and at boot (cases E and I).
- [ ] The offer carries a third choice to pick a different folder (the folder chooser of #352), and its text has no icon or glyph drawn between its two sentences: a 640x480 frame from guest d and, when it is next staged, one from the device.
- [ ] The words the offer uses are approved by the maintainer before the build (`player-language.md`): proposed `YOUR CLOUD HAS NO /ROCKNIX/Saves FOLDER YET.` / `CREATE IT`, `CHOOSE A FOLDER`, `NOT NOW`; their French lands in the same commit (D-UI-051).
- [ ] The default folder's name (`/ROCKNIX` today, D-WORKFLOW-101; `/pixelelated` proposed) is a register row on the maintainer's word, with D-WORKFLOW-101's mixed-installation test run before any default changes.



## The maintainer, later the same evening (the timing)

> Beyond just the scan, we also need to make sure that the directory checking is happening after adding a new rclone remote backend, and not showing on start-up like it did for me. Maybe it was the auto sync game saves that caused that prompt to appear, but it was unexpected there and is much more helpful to be shown during the cloud setup process.

Read: the offer came from the startup saves sync (`GuiCloudTransfer.cpp:297` presents whatever `cloud_restore` printed as `>>> offer`), which is the case they met. The timing checkbox above is rewritten to their words: the check belongs to cloud setup, after the remote is added; the syncs only report.



## Decided 2026-10-01 (D-CLOUD-165): the set-aside moves too

> I agree with your recommendation. Let's migrate that as well. For a user, we want the process to feel seamless, and their expectation would be that things kept working and that this was more of a cosmetic shift than a functional one.

- [ ] The move carries `Saves-replaced` (the set-aside of conflict losers beside the saves folder) to `/pixelelated/Saves-replaced` by the same copy, verify, delete, and nothing of ours remains under the old name afterwards: a `tools/last-good-scripts-test` case seeds a set-aside copy under the old layout and reads it back under the new one with the old folder gone; the round trip on the VM shows the sync's next set-aside landing under `/pixelelated`.


P4 audit contract reconciliation, 2026-10-06: the wording above now states the existing D-CLOUD-173 boot exception explicitly (audit B-04, narrowed to contract reconciliation). This changes no runtime requirement, completion state, historical title or checkbox. Source trace: EmulationStation `main.cpp` startup preparation before receive/send; the original runtime prohibition was withdrawn by the verified Fable refutation. Current candidate qualification remains tracked by #471.

full_comments.body:
Added by D-CLOUD-158 (the default folder is `/Rasteratops`):

- [ ] The sweep of the old words: `tools/archaeology --reversal /ROCKNIX/Saves` lists every rule, register row and document naming `/ROCKNIX` as the cloud root; each is reworded to `/Rasteratops` or marked as history in the same change as the code, and the command then prints only history (`decision-register.md` § A reversal sweeps its old words).

**Placement, 2026-10-01 (D-CLOUD-159).** The maintainer: *"let's move everything to \"/Rasteratops\" as the default root directory we look for. that should be part of our baseline brand transition"*. So the default itself lands with #337's identity change in the same candidate; this epic's #353 keeps the migrations (a carried `/GAMES` re-pointed without a question; the fork's earlier `/ROCKNIX` read and offered the move) and the guards. The Nova's one-line re-point to `/ROCKNIX/Saves` is withdrawn as moot; its cloud moves to `/Rasteratops` with the candidate, on a yes asked by name.

**Answers, 2026-10-01 (questions 1 and 2 of 5, D-CLOUD-160 and D-CLOUD-161).** An earlier `/ROCKNIX` is moved on one question, MOVE first (copy, verify, then delete; safe to interrupt; the other devices follow when they next check). A carried upstream `/GAMES` is treated as no folder: the device is asked whether to create `/Rasteratops` with its sync folders, the same offer the setup step makes; a `/GAMES` that actually holds files gets the move dialog naming it. The silent re-point criterion above is superseded by these; the body is edited in the same action.

## Phase 1 design, from the reads (2026-10-01)

What exists: `cloud_migrate_layout` already moves a device off an old layout by copy, verify (`rclone check`, whole output read), then delete, refuses a merge into a non-empty target, resumes a cut-short copy, and is driven from the cloud storage page by its `--check` output (`GuiMenu.cpp:5158-5230`); `cloud_sync_helper` carries keys and superseded *numbers* across an upgrade (`migrate_default`) but leaves a carried `/GAMES` alone by design; `cloud_setup --seed-folders` makes the configured folders at the end of the wizard; `cloud_restore` prints `>>> offer create-saves-folder` when the saves folder is absent and its parent lists.

The changes, each a small edit to that machinery:

1. **Defaults** (D-CLOUD-158/159): `/Rasteratops/{Saves,Backups,Content}` in `cloud_sync.conf`, `.defaults`, `cloud_setup`'s fallbacks and `cloud_migrate_layout`'s `NEW_*`.
2. **Superseded defaults are not "a layout of your own"**: `cloud_migrate_layout` keeps a list of the defaults it ever shipped (`/GAMES` and `/ROCKNIX/Saves` with their siblings); a device whose saves folder equals one is offered the move (today the sibling-layout branch returns "nothing to move" for `/ROCKNIX`); any other folder stays the player's own (D-CLOUD-160's KEEP is implicit there).
3. **Layout state as a verb**: `cloud_setup --layout-state` prints `STATE=current | superseded-empty | superseded-with-files | own | no-remote` with the folders named, so the interface decides without parsing prose: `superseded-with-files` → the MOVE / KEEP USING / NOT NOW dialog (D-CLOUD-160); `superseded-empty` → the create-`/Rasteratops` offer (D-CLOUD-161); `current` and `own` → nothing. KEEP writes `LAYOUT_KEEP=<folder>` to the conf (asked once); NOT NOW writes nothing (asked again at the next setup or scan).
4. **Following**: in `cloud_restore`'s absent-folder path, a superseded default whose current-default sibling already exists in the cloud (another device moved) is re-pointed without a question, with a journal line; the offer, where it still applies, names the current default.
5. **Where it is asked**: the cloud setup page's completion step and the scan page (#350), never the startup or exit sync, whose card ends with an action line pointing at MANAGE CLOUD STORAGE when the folder is a superseded default (the timing rule on this issue).
6. **The marker** (#356): `cloud_migrate_layout` writes `/Rasteratops/.layout` (`layout=2`) after a move or a seeding; a device reads it before offering anything.

Proofs on `tools/vm-pair` and `tools/cloud-round-trip` as the criteria say; the interface half (the dialog, the scan page) follows the script half.

**From the futro (2026-10-01), two criteria added ahead of the interface work:**

- [ ] `cloud_migrate_layout --state` looks for every superseded default's folder in the cloud, not only the configured one: a device configured for `/GAMES` whose cloud holds `/ROCKNIX/Saves` with files reads `STATE=superseded-with-files` with `SOURCE=/ROCKNIX/Saves`, and the move dialog, not the creation, is offered (the Nova's real case: its conf names `/GAMES`, its saves sit in `/ROCKNIX/Saves`); a sandbox check in `tools/last-good-scripts-test` section aa fails against the verb as first written.
- [ ] `--follow` refuses to re-point a device whose old folder still holds files the new folder lacks: it reads `superseded-with-files` and the move is offered instead; the `tools/cloud-round-trip` move case seeds a save into the old folder after the move and shows the second device offered, not followed, with the save intact.
- [ ] `Saves-replaced` (the set-aside of conflict losers beside the saves folder) moves with the saves, or the notes say it stays under the old name -- the maintainer's call, asked in the futro's report.

**Phase 1, the script half, landed on `feature/cloud-epic` at `48c2df30a9` (2026-10-01).** The defaults are `/Rasteratops/{Saves,Backups,Content}`; `cloud_migrate_layout` knows the superseded defaults (`/GAMES`, `/ROCKNIX/Saves`), offers the move for them, and gains `--state`, `--keep`, `--follow`, `--superseded` and the `.layout` marker (#356); the sync scripts follow the fleet before writing. `tools/last-good-scripts-test`: PASSED (1403 lines) with the new section aa (15 checks; 12 fail against the old tool) and sections x, y, z moved to the new default. Still open from the futro before the interface reads the verb: the state verb's look across every superseded folder (the Nova's `/GAMES`-in-conf, `/ROCKNIX`-in-cloud case) and the follow's refusal when the old folder holds newer files -- next.

**The futro's two criteria, the script side, at `1de43faa25`.** `--state` looks across every superseded default's folder and names the one holding files (`SOURCE=`); `--check`/`--apply` move from it; `--follow` refuses while the old folder holds files. Section aa of `tools/last-good-scripts-test` carries both (twenty checks; three fail against `48c2df30a9`); the suite PASSED at 1407 lines. The criteria themselves were posted as a comment (not in the body), so there is nothing to tick in the list above yet; the round-trip half of the follow's proof waits for the VM run.

**The set-aside moves too, at `79aa0b28e4` (D-CLOUD-165).** `relocate` takes a folder with no pointer; the move carries `<saves>-replaced` after the saves; `--check` lists it. The suite's local-backend case moves `/ROCKNIX/Saves-replaced/<stamp>/gb/L.srm` to `/Rasteratops/Saves-replaced/…`, leaves nothing under `/ROCKNIX`, and reads `layout=2` back; PASSED at 1409 lines. The criterion's VM half (the sync's next set-aside landing under `/Rasteratops`) waits for the round trip.

**The interface half, at ES `dc819f432` and scripts `b221d9e142` (D-CLOUD-166/167).** The scan page that opens both transfer pages reads `cloud_migrate_layout --state` and raises, before anything is offered:

- `superseded-with-files` (the fork's earlier `/ROCKNIX`, or upstream's `/GAMES`, holds saves and no current folder exists): YOUR CLOUD HAS A /ROCKNIX FOLDER FROM AN EARLIER VERSION. MOVE IT TO /Rasteratops? YOUR OTHER DEVICES WILL FOLLOW. -- MOVE / KEEP USING /ROCKNIX / NOT NOW. MOVE runs `--apply` on its own page, MOVING YOUR CLOUD FOLDER: the script now announces each tier (`>>> unit SAVES|i|n`, SETTINGS BACKUPS, DISCARDED SAVES, the content) and its steps (`>>> doing copy|verify|remove` -> COPYING..., CHECKING THE COPY..., REMOVING THE OLD FOLDER...), streaming the copy's progress; a move that could not finish reads COULDN'T FINISH - <why> with YOUR CLOUD STILL HAS /ROCKNIX. NOTHING WAS REMOVED. and TRY AGAIN beside CLOSE; one that did is dismissed by the player and scans again. KEEP USING runs `--keep`; NOT NOW asks next time.
- `superseded-empty`, or no current folder on a restore: YOUR CLOUD HAS NO /Rasteratops FOLDER YET. CREATE IT, WITH FOLDERS FOR SAVES, SETTINGS BACKUPS, AND GAME CONTENT? -- CREATE IT (the re-point, then `--seed-folders`, on a page that goes on by itself) / CHOOSE A FOLDER (the CLOUD FOLDER keyboard) / NOT NOW.
- a superseded, empty folder beside a current one that exists is followed inside the scan, with no question (D-CLOUD-160's "your other devices will follow").

And the automatic card (D-CLOUD-166): a startup or exit sync with no saves folder says SKIPPED - YOUR CLOUD FOLDER ISN'T SET UP YET with SET IT UP: GAME SETTINGS > MANAGE CLOUD STORAGE, stamps `CloudExit::NoFolder` (78) so the row under SYNC SAVES DURING STARTUP says the same, and raises no dialog -- the screen the maintainer met on the Nova at startup. The scripts are unchanged there (exit 0 and the offer line); the card reads the offer for its automatic origins.

Can this be done on the VM? **Yes** -- `tools/vm-pair` with guest a on this cut and guest b on RC2, the WebDAV seeded with `/ROCKNIX/{Saves,Backups,Content,Saves-replaced}` and a `/GAMES` conf on a; the frames at 640x480 of each dialog and page; the move's `rclone check` read from the backend. That proof is next, before the pin bump.

**The mixed-installation test (D-CLOUD-158's gate, D-WORKFLOW-101 row 4) ran on `tools/vm-pair`, and the second device's move is a merge now (D-CLOUD-168, `49b2baddba`).**

The test (`epic-mixed-pair.sh`, 15:40 UTC): guest a on run 95's image (`92c6cf25f1`), guest b on RC2's (`69e6039f8f`), one QA WebDAV seeded with `/ROCKNIX/Saves/nes/Probe.srm`, both devices configured for `/ROCKNIX`.

1. b (the old build) restores from `/ROCKNIX`, adds a save, backs up: its save is in `/ROCKNIX/Saves`. PASS.
2. a (this cut) reads `superseded-with-files` and moves: both saves under `/Rasteratops`, `/ROCKNIX/Saves` gone, the marker written, a re-pointed. PASS.
3. b keeps playing on the old build: a new save goes up under `/ROCKNIX/Saves`, which comes back with three files; a's next restore does not see it. PASS -- the split D-CLOUD-160 accepts until b moves, recorded.
3b. a changes `Probe.srm` and backs it up: the two folders now hold a differing version of one save.
4. The second device's move (a's conf pointed back at `/ROCKNIX`, as b's reads after its upgrade): `--state` reads `superseded-with-files` with `CURRENT_EXISTS=1` and the marker; `--follow` refuses (3), since the old folder holds files; `--apply` **used to refuse** (`REFUSING: /Rasteratops/Saves already exists`, the futro's pre-mortem) and now merges: the differing `Probe.srm` is shelved first under `/Rasteratops/Saves-replaced/<stamp>-move/`, the copy runs with `--update` and `--backup-dir` on that shelf, the old folder is removed once every name is present. After it: `/Rasteratops/Saves` holds `FromB2.srm` beside the fleet's two, the fleet's newer `Probe.srm` is the one kept, the old folder's copy is on the shelf, nothing under `/ROCKNIX`. PASS (10 of 10).

The gate is the fleet's marker (`.layout`): a `/Rasteratops` with no marker is somebody's own folder and is still refused. Four sandbox cases in `last-good-scripts-test` section aa cover the refusal, the `--check` wording, the merge's commands and the shelf. **D-CLOUD-168 is a fork resolved under D-CLOUD-160's "your other devices will follow", for the maintainer to confirm or reverse**; the shelf is pruned to one generation by the next backup like every set-aside.

Also from the guest-d proof of run 95 (`docs/qa-frames/2026-10-01/354/`): the move dialog, the move page, the create offer and the startup card's SKIPPED line are as approved; CREATE IT on a carried stock conf (`CONTENT_REMOTE=""`) seeded ROMs and BIOS at the cloud's root -- an empty content pointer now follows the saves to `/Rasteratops/Content` (`49b2baddba`).

**Code trace** (D-WORKFLOW-050, for the candidate's preflight): the folder's state is `cloud_migrate_layout --state` (`744c4dcee6`, `b221d9e142`): every default this project ever shipped (`SUPERSEDED_DEFAULT_SAVES`: `/GAMES`, `/ROCKNIX/Saves`) is looked at and the one holding files is the move's source, so a device set to `/GAMES` whose cloud holds `/ROCKNIX/Saves` reads `superseded-with-files` naming it. `cloud_scan` runs the verb when BACK UP TO THE CLOUD or RESTORE FROM THE CLOUD opens (ES `dc819f432`, `cloudOpenTransfer`), follows the fleet in the scan when the old folder is empty and the current one exists, and `cloudOfferFolder` raises the move dialog (`superseded-with-files`) or the create offer (`superseded-empty`, or no current folder on a restore). MOVE runs `--apply` on a page; onto a current folder another device made (the `.layout` marker) it merges, newer wins, the differing versions shelved first under `<saves>-replaced/<stamp>-move` (`49b2baddba`, D-CLOUD-168); CREATE IT runs the re-point and `cloud_setup --seed-folders`, with an empty content pointer carried to `/Rasteratops/Content`. The automatic syncs raise no dialog: `ThreadedCloudSync` reads the scripts' offer on a startup or exit origin as `SKIPPED - YOUR CLOUD FOLDER ISN'T SET UP YET`, stamped `78 no-folder` (ES `dc819f432`, D-CLOUD-166).

Already written: a device upgraded from stock carries `SAVES_REMOTE="/GAMES"`, `SETTINGS_REMOTE="/GAMES/backup"`, `CONTENT_REMOTE=""` (the Nova, read 2026-09-30) -- read as before by `cloud_sync_helper`, never rewritten by it; the scan reads that conf and the cloud together, so the Nova is offered the move from `/ROCKNIX/Saves` (where its saves are), not a `/GAMES` creation. A device on the fork's earlier `/ROCKNIX` keeps syncing there until it answers the dialog (KEEP USING keeps it for good, `LAYOUT_KEEP`); its `Saves-replaced` set-aside moves with its saves (D-CLOUD-165). Nothing in any cloud changes until MOVE or CREATE IT is pressed; a startup on the old folder with the current one already made is re-pointed by the follow, which refuses while the old folder holds files (the futro's rule). The kept core of the verb's crash and the debug binary were deleted from guest d.

Three acceptance criteria rewritten in the body to the decisions made since: a carried `/GAMES` is settled silently by the seeding at the end of setup (D-CLOUD-169) and offered CREATE IT by the cloud folder step at boot (D-CLOUD-170); another device follows at its step or a transfer page's scan rather than before a sync, and one that wrote into the old folder first is merged by its MOVE (D-CLOUD-168, D-CLOUD-170); and the folder is settled by the step at the end of setup and at boot, never by a sync (D-CLOUD-166, D-CLOUD-170, #363). Each now names the frame or suite line that ticks it; run 100 (`cb0b051b72`) is building and its guest-d proof carries the cases named (B0, B, E, I, L).

The simulation says: the move page's words must tell the player to leave the other devices alone for the minutes it runs, and the P3 order must stage all three before any move.
- It reads `STATE=superseded-empty` on the Nova (whose `/GAMES` is absent) and offers CREATE IT, which seeds `/Rasteratops` -- while the Nova's real saves sit in `/ROCKNIX/Saves`, which `--state` never looked at because the Nova's conf names `/GAMES`. **The Nova is both superseded-empty (by its conf) and a `/ROCKNIX` device (by its cloud).** The state verb must look for *every* superseded default's folder in the cloud, not only the configured one, and prefer the move over the creation when one holds files. Today's `SAVES_EXCLUDES` excludes `/backup/**` and `/Backups/**` only; `Saves-replaced` sits beside `Saves`, not inside it, so the move leaves it in `/ROCKNIX` -- orphaned under the old name, never deleted, never read. Entered if it recurs; named here.

**Replaced-mechanism archetype.** The startup-sync offer (`>>> offer create-saves-folder` presented by `GuiCloudTransfer`) is replaced by the setup step and the scan page. What it guarded: a fresh device whose cloud has no folder got asked at the first boot with the cloud reachable. A device that signed in, declined, and never opens the pages keeps a card with an action line every boot -- which is the design (D-CLOUD-153's timing rule), and the notes say so.

- [x] D-CLOUD-178/179 and the implemented diagram define selected-category checks/creation, independent paths and manual content guidance; prospective repairs are separately identified with #515 ownership.

>
> I feel like we arrived at a good solution that relied on post-rclone remote setup. At the time, verification, directory creation, and user actions could live, so someone could help tidy up certain elements while we provide documentation for how to handle more data-intensive operations.

> If we don't have it institutionalized already as a required process, we need to make sure that any time we make any change to EmulationStation or any part of our information architecture (or even screen content), we update the flow and then the accompanying screenshot for the flow. This is going to be increasingly critical as we work on automated testing.

> We also ensured that we updated all of our documentation and our diagrams that serve as canonical reference points for all of the flows and information architecture of the app. The idea was also to use these as a way to store screenshots at each flow, so we know what the definitive happy path flows are and also what the branching edge cases are. We have a visual benchmark and baseline for what the entire experience throughout EmulationStation is meant to be.

> Sounds good, and we should trigger a new lane if you want, within Herdr, for website work. I want to keep us focused here in this lane on the critical path of getting the build completed. We were in the flow, trying to get everything done. Run the changes and adjustments for the release candidate to simplify the experience and expectations of what happens when connecting a new remote via rclone, and I don't want to lose that progress and momentum.

If they happen to choose a different folder, I didn't think we would move their ROMs around. If we need to add more clarity to our own flows and what tidying up is, we should think more about that. We could let the user select a different directory for their ROMs, or we could create the structure and instruct them to move their ROMs into the folder that's waiting for them.
>
> With the tidying up, we should think about what that does, because I actually don't remember right now if it touches ROM files at all and how it's currently structured or not. If we restrict it just to game saves, save states, and screenshots, that might be fine.
>
> Again, no one has used anything we've built, including what was opened as PRs to ROCKNIX, so they'll be coming from the current version of ROCKNIX. No one will be upgrading like I am, so we should not do anything to accommodate me. The only thing we should do is revert or clean up my folder after we attempted to do the migration from /ROCKNIX to /pixelelated.

> Well, another option is to create the folder and use it for the bits we enable. If they'd like to use it for ROMs, we should then make a decision about whether they would need to move their ROMs into that directory first or choose their own.
>
> For simplicity's sake, we might just say that once you link an Arcclone backend, we create the structure for them and then ask them to move things into those directories. All our tool does is give away that, once they've migrated the content in, it validates it. At that point, we could tidy things up because everything's already in the directory, so we shouldn't be moving anything around.
>
> Alternatively, we could offer strictly the tidy-up, save states, game saves, and screenshots. Another option would be to tell them what's not passing and have it be a series of checks. If they want to fix it, we could offer the option to fix that content type. This would be similar to what we do with the restore, where we let them choose from several options. We would just allow them to organize and let them select what they want to organize, and then the burden is on the user, not on us.

> Yes, this is where I think a validator is probably the way to go. Now we can offer a fix for smaller file types, and then we can deal with some edge cases that we know will likely happen. For example, if the ROMs aren't present at all, or if they're not in the right directory but present, I think the same would be true for the BIOS files. We can then also point them to look online for documentation on how to set everything up for those two types.

> A validator would also be helpful, and we may actually already have the building blocks in our restore and backup functions because we already have interface elements and checks around this.

> We also shouldn't have a link that is expected to be clickable. We could show a QR code, though.

> We need to build out our site, so this can be a future task we define now and tackle later. Once the site's live, we could have this on the wiki. It would take someone directly to the setup guide, and we could then have one for their ROMs and one for BIOS files. Instead of a fix button, it would say "See instructions" or something akin to that, and that would then show a QR code in a modal to take them to the page to fix it.

#515's ten-case review traces actual public ROCKNIX and packaged writers.
